text:
nina: heads-up — canary v12 (gpt-lite) is showing ~18% p99 token-latency regression vs v11 on /chat. saw it on the token-level dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/perf/token-breakdown?canary=v12 :eyes:
ana: grabbing the graph now. token breakdown shows a clear spike in KV_LOOKUP time for first ~8 tokens, kernel_exec looks slightly higher too but KV is dominant.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started: v12 -> 5% traffic at 2026-02-14T10:23Z (id: canary-20260214-5pct)
sam: ran an offline profile on a representative request (seq=24). flamegraph indicates kernel selector falling back to generic_matmul for the small-seq path. suspect kernel_tuner returning no optimized kernel for M=128,N=64 for short sequences. snippet from perf log:

```
# profiler excerpt
kernel_selector: try optimized_matmul_fast->failed (score=0.0)
kernel_selector: fallback -> generic_matmul
kernel_exec: generic_matmul  1.8ms (p50) / 9.6ms (p99)
kv_lookup: 12.4ms (p99) for token 2
```

kai: related: batching heuristics are sharding these short-seq requests into the "low-latency pool" which uses smaller micro-batches. that reduces kernel amortization on matmul; combined with the fallback to generic kernel we get the regression. iirc the route tag logic ignored routes missing the `x-seq-hint` header so a handful landed in the wrong pool.
nina: we also saw KV cache miss-rate tick up on v12 canary in the last hour. any chance serialization change affected key order/namespace?
sam: good catch — i dumped a few KV keys. v11 keys: `['dialog:1234:kv','dialog:1234:prefix']` but v12 produced `['dialog:1234:prefix','dialog:1234:kv']` — that reordering breaks our prefix heuristic for prefetching, causing more RPCs.
opsbot: alert: route=/chat token_p99 > 500ms for 10m (rule: perf/token_p99_route)
nana: for dashboards — proposal: add per-route per-model-version token-latency heatmap (tokens on x, time on y) plus stacked columns for token_latency.breakdown = {kv_lookup,kernel_exec,scheduling,network}. also add a delta panel comparing model_v11 vs model_v12 using canary tag and show relative % change per-token. example PromQL-ish query I will implement in the panel config:

```
# pseudocode query
sum by(token_index,component) (rate(token_latency_bucket{canary=~"v11|v12",route="/chat"}[5m]))
```

kai: sounds good. minimal change suggestion: relax routing gate to also consider `content-length` and fallback to the medium-batch pool for seq<=48 until kernel_tuner bug is fixed. will open a small config PR.
sam: action item — i'll add a reproducer that forces the kernel_tuner selection path, and run a microbenchmark across MxN spaces. if we can get optimized_matmul to return a positive score for the common short-seq shapes we should recover most of the perf.
nina: action items roundup: 1) ana add heatmap & per-version compare panels + link here; 2) kai patch routing heuristics to catch missing header and route to medium-batch pool; 3) sam produce reproducer + kernel_tuner patch or fallback tuning; 4) sam also verify KV key serialization ordering and fix prefetch prefixing if needed; 5) if p99 doesn't drop below 10% regression in 30m i'll rollback canary to 0% (deploy-bot: rollback ready).
nana: :thumbsup: i'll spin up the dashboard PR now and attach screenshots. aiming to have panels live in 20-30m.
sam: reproducer + perf traces will be in this thread shortly. sharing a perf trace link when ready.
nina: thx everyone — keeping notes here for A/B comparison later. please paste short notes/results back in this thread (one-line updates preferred).
